design.md's ## Test Strategy (187-222) is otherwise exceptionally thorough: it states an exhaustive AC-to-TEST coverage table (195-210, 14 rows for AC-001..AC-014 matching all 14 TEST-001..TEST-014 IDs 1:1) plus a REQ-to-AC roll-up (line 193) that I independently verified is complete and accurate against requirements.md's six REQ sections. Every 'Delivered by' cell resolves to a concrete, named artifact elsewhere in the document (a specific table, a specific numbered item, or a specific Stream B deliverable), not a bare self-reference -- a real plan, not a lookup index, for 13 of 14 rows. However, item 1's elaboration of AC-003/TEST-003 (design.md:212) directly contradicts acceptance-tests.md and reproduces a defect requirements-side review already caught and fixed. design.md:212: 'Unset, empty, 600, 1, 0, -5, abc. First three proceed; last three exit 2 before the CLI is invoked.' Against this 7-item list, 'first three' (unset, empty, 600) plus 'last three' (0, -5, abc) leaves the 4th item, 1, unclassified -- exactly the error acceptance-tests.md:43 records as previously caught: 'An earlier draft wrote first three / last three against a seven-item list, leaving 1 unclassified. Both round-2 reviewers caught the arithmetic independently.' acceptance-tests.md:40 states the corrected grouping: 'First four (unset, empty, 600, 1): the runner proceeds to invoke the CLI. 1 is a valid bound, not an invalid one -- it is the same value AC-004's timeout sub-cases use.' design.md's own AC-004 elaboration (item 2, line 214) independently relies on SDD_PANELIST_TIMEOUT=1 as a valid, accepted bound, so item 1's unrepaired arithmetic is also internally inconsistent with item 2 in the same section. Concrete failure mode: an implementer following design.md's Test Strategy item 1 literally has no correct instruction for the 1 sub-case of TEST-003 -- the same value item 2 depends on being accepted rather than rejected. This is the identical defect class (a plan reading well against headings while silently carrying a stale/incorrect AC-level detail) that produced attempt 1's three-round BLOCKED escalation, now recurring one level inside the very coverage table built to prevent it.
